activities.anchor: A second classification matters for policy
activities.caption: file each pollutant: emitted, or manufactured in the air
activities.name: aqaPrimaryBuckets

config.prompt: Primary vs secondary pollutants — file each one:

items.label: sulfur dioxide from sulfur in coal and oil
nitrogen oxides from every hot flame
ground-level ozone, cooked from NO₂ plus volatile organics by sunlight

config.why: Controlling smog means controlling its ingredients, not the smog itself — effective regulation targets nodes in the reaction network, not symptoms.

activities.anchor: The dose–response evidence has a famous natural experiment
activities.caption: call the effect — the Six Cities gap
activities.name: aqaSixCitiesEstimate

config.prompt: The Harvard Six Cities study followed thousands of residents for decades. Roughly how much higher was the most-polluted city's death rate than the cleanest's?
config.why: Roughly 26% higher, driven by fine particles — the result that established PM2.5 as the regulatory target and survived two decades of replication.
config.context: There is no demonstrated safe threshold, which is why the WHO's 2021 guideline (5 µg/m³) sits far below most cities' reality.

activities.anchor: Trust the monitors, not the view
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the crisp morning
activities.name: aqaClearPredict

config.q: A crisp sunny morning: the air looks perfectly clear. Is it clean?
choices: Yes — if you can see clearly, you can breathe safely
Not necessarily — the deadliest common pollutant is invisible
config.why: PM2.5 is far below the size the eye resolves, and a visible plume may be mostly nuisance dust — indoor solid-fuel smoke kills in homes where the air outside looks clear.

activities.anchor: which is why air-quality agencies employ more meteorologists than chemists
activities.caption: the forecast desk — what dominates this week?
activities.name: aqaWeatherBranch

config.root: You are on the city's air-quality forecast desk. The emissions inventory is unchanged; the weather is not.

start.text: Which situation are you forecasting for?

choices.label: A winter high-pressure system, mountain-ringed city
A hot, still, sunny summer afternoon

inversion.text: A warm layer sits over cooler air: cold, polluted air is trapped beneath the lid like smoke under glass — London 1952 and Donora 1948 were built this way.

wind.text: Calm concentrates; wind disperses. The same emissions, a different week, a different city.

photochem.text: Ozone needs sunlight, so its worst days are hot, still and sunny — afternoon peaks built from morning traffic, with the mixing height deepest at midday.

config.why: The weather comes first and the chemistry second — that is why agencies staff more meteorologists than chemists.

activities.caption: pair each casualty with its mechanism
activities.name: aqaAcidMatch

config.prompt: Acid rain's three targets — pair system with damage:

pairs.right: acidification kills fish below about pH 5; the eggs fail first
acid strips nutrients and mobilises aluminium, damaging root systems
limestone and marble dissolve — the visible pitting on a century of cathedrals
died from British smoke — pollution ignores borders

config.why: The fix: cap the total, price the tonne, let engineers find the cheapest tonnes — cutting acid rain emissions about half at a fraction of predicted cost.

activities.caption: fill the blanks — the ozone hole's mechanism
activities.name: aqaOzoneCloze

config.text: CFCs are stable enough to reach the stratosphere, where %%0%% cracks them and frees chlorine atoms; one chlorine atom then catalytically destroys %%1%% of ozone molecules. The 1985 Antarctic measurements found springtime ozone down by %%2%% — far worse than models predicted, because polar stratospheric clouds supercharged the chemistry.
config.hint: The Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs — the first treaty ratified by every country on Earth.

activities.anchor: and the hole does not heat the planet
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the radio caller
activities.name: aqaCallerSpot

config.prompt: A radio caller explains the two atmospheric problems — one line is faulty, click it:
lines: The ozone hole is chlorine chemistry from CFCs.
Climate change is infrared absorption by CO₂, methane and friends.
So the hole is caused by CO₂ — closing it would cool the planet.
The genuine coupling runs the other way: HFC substitutes are potent greenhouse gases.
Your air conditioner does not open the hole.
config.correction: Two problems, two causes, no arrow between them — the hole is chlorine chemistry, the warming is infrared absorption.
config.why: The one genuine coupling runs the other way — the same treaty family now covers both, with Kigali phasing down HFCs.

activities.anchor: Here is the subtlety that makes air quality and climate entangled
activities.caption: two particles, opposite climates — drag between them
activities.name: aqaAerosolCompare

config.prompt: Aerosols pull both ways — drag the divider:

before.label: sulfate aerosols
before.text: Scatter sunlight back to space and brighten cloud droplets — cooling, and masking part of the greenhouse signal (why 1950–1980 warmed less than physics predicted).

after.label: black carbon (soot)
after.text: Absorbs sunlight and warms; darkens snow and ice on landing, accelerating melt — the Himalayan brown cloud is partly a glacier problem, not just a lung problem.

config.why: Net across all aerosols: a substantial cooling. Cleaning the air saves lives now — and the un-masked warming is paid the only way warming can be paid, by cutting CO₂.
